text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.6% today as crude oil prices spiked to their highest levels in six months, driven by escalating Middle East tensions and threats of U.S. military action against Iran. Brent crude topped $116 a barrel—well above the $107–$115 range the market was trading in just days earlier—and this sharp move directly lifts profits for oil producers like ConocoPhillips, which earn more when the commodity they pump commands higher prices.

The broader backdrop is a shift in global energy markets triggered by regional conflict: supply uncertainty, combined with reports that the U.S. is preparing strikes on Iran and withdrawing diplomatic staff from Saudi Arabia, has made oil a beneficiary of geopolitical risk. The stock's 12% gain over two weeks reflects this same tailwind—oil has been climbing as investors price in both immediate supply disruption risk and longer-term changes to which countries and companies benefit from higher energy costs.
